calibration: No drawing. About 54 px/m locally in the oblique photograph, checked by the 2.69 m body depth.

comparisons: Side and three-quarter renders inspected against the photographs by eye. No overlay or matched camera was possible with the evidence found.
corrections: Generic wing and stub nacelles replaced with a high wing on long nacelles carrying the main gear.
Nacelles reduced from a first pass 1.7 m deep and 9.6 m long to 1.48 m and 8.9 m, and the propeller plane moved forward, after the line-up and the underside photograph.
Seated eye moved from u 4.00 to 3.15 and h 2.02, forward in the side pane where G-ECOG shows the pilot. No published eye position was found, so this is an estimate.
Window top lowered 0.05 m, sill lowered about 0.06 m, and the stray post from 2.30 to 2.42 removed: G-ECOG shows two panes a side.

Kit changes: glass clear from the seat and tinted from outside, as on the Bendy airliner. The thick glareshield slab and its large FLIGHT GUIDANCE lettering are replaced by a thin sloped hood with a rolled lip over a slim mode control strip. The panel, floor and overhead take their reach from the nose skin, and a dark coaming lines the inside of the nose.

limitations: Lowest-confidence type with the CJ4: no dimensioned drawing was found. Nose, tail-cone and fin tables are reconstructions read by eye from oblique photographs.
Static attitude of 0.5 degrees and keel height are estimates. Model height runs slightly over the published figure.
Wing planform is scaled to the published area, not traced.
Exterior only: shared interior, refitted but not compared with a Dash 8 flight deck.
Eye station and window limits are estimated from an oblique photograph, not measured.
Sanity pass only: seating, glass and visibility. The panel, hood and pedestal remain the shared kit interior fitted to the nose, not compared with this type's real flight deck.
